Hearty

HAR-tee -- two syllables, stress on the first syllable, HAR. Careful: it sounds close to 'hardy,' a different word. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Hearty is loudly vigorous and cheerful.

Grandpa's hearty singing carried over the whole campfire.

Worked Example

The coach does not just say congratulations. His 'WELL DONE!' booms across the gym, his handshake rattles your arm, and his laugh arrives before the door finishes opening.

Everything about the coach is hearty: loudly vigorous and cheerful, with real force behind the warmth. Hearty describes cheer with muscle in it -- booming greetings, roaring cheers, back-slapping congratulations.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

vigorous: strong, energetic, and forceful

jolly: cheerful and good-humored

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

faint: weak and barely noticeable

glum: silent and gloomy in mood

Where it sits · how much force joins the cheerfulness — jolly → hearty → vigorous

jolly vs. hearty: Jolly covers the cheerful half only -- a jolly mood can be quiet -- while hearty adds volume and force: a hearty welcome arrives at full strength.

vigorous vs. hearty: Vigorous is the strongest on pure energy -- a vigorous workout has no cheer in it at all -- while hearty keeps the energy and the warmth: loud, strong, and glad to see you.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — heart

root — heart: the heart (Old English heorte)

suffix — -y

suffix — -y: full of (Old English -ig)

Put it together

Put it together: Hearty is literally 'full of heart' -- cheer and strength pumped straight from the chest, which is why hearty laughs, cheers, and welcomes all come out at full volume.

Use the root in a new word: hearten

Use the root in a new word: hearten: The rescue crew was heartened by the sound of tapping from below.

Root Check

Word Choice

Hearty describes cheer delivered with force: a hearty laugh, welcome, cheer, or handshake. Two traps to know: hearty also describes filling food (a hearty stew), a separate everyday sense; and do not confuse hearty with hardy, which means tough enough to survive -- a hardy plant, but a hearty greeting.
